# remove-markdown 0.8.2

This patch fixes a case where stripping Markdown deleted a web address from
prose. In 0.8.1, `Visit <https://example.com>.` became `Visit .`. Version
0.8.2 removes the angle brackets and returns `Visit https://example.com.`.
The fix applies by default to both HTTP and HTTPS. It keeps the URL's original
spelling, including punctuation in paths, query strings and fragments.

| Markdown input | 0.8.1 output | 0.8.2 output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<b>Visit <https://example.com>.</b>` | `Visit .` | `Visit https://example.com.` |
| `<https://example.com/a_*b*?q=1#top>` | Empty string | `https://example.com/a_*b*?q=1#top` |
| `<a href="https://example.com">Notes</a>` | `Notes` | `Notes` |

The converter still strips ordinary HTML. Addresses inside HTML attributes,
HTML comments and recognized code spans or code blocks follow the same rules
as in 0.8.1.

With default options, 32 of 2,108 real Markdown files produced different
output. Over the same corpus, the median paired increase in conversion time
was 2.6%. Among the 42 files containing a potential web autolink, the median
increase was 18%. A synthetic file alternating code and prose URLs took
2.32 times as long as in 0.8.1. [Regression tests and benchmarks in PR #146](https://github.com/zuchka/remove-markdown/pull/146)

```sh
npm install remove-markdown@0.8.2
```
